meta.location: Zarahemla; the land of Melek; the city of Ammonihah

world_behind.title: The record stops to explain a naming rule
world_behind.text: Verse 7 gives the Nephite custom outright: lands, cities and villages are called after the name of whoever first possessed them. It is a piece of civil convention dropped into a travel narrative, and it is supplied at the exact moment the reader meets a place name that will matter.

world_behind.title: The place where it worked gets four verses
world_behind.text: Everyone came, everyone was baptized, and the whole episode is disposed of in four verses with no opposition, no argument and no names. Twenty-six verses then go to the town that threw him out.

world_behind.title: Ammonihah knows exactly who he is
world_behind.text: They name his office, name the church he founded, name the man he handed the bench to, and draw the correct legal conclusion. This is not ignorance refusing a stranger; it is a briefed city refusing a man whose jurisdiction it has checked.

world_behind.title: The resignation is quoted back at him as a defence
world_behind.text: Four chapters ago Alma gave up the judgment-seat so he could preach. Here the people of Ammonihah cite that same act to prove he has no power over them. The decision that freed him to come is the reason they can throw him out.

world_behind.title: The angel says it is the same angel
world_behind.text: Verse 15 has the messenger identify himself as the one who delivered Alma's first message. That puts the being on the road to Ammonihah and the being who stopped him on the road to destroy the church in the same person, about twenty years apart.

world_behind.title: Amulek was told first
world_behind.text: Verse 20 has him recognise Alma before Alma says a word, because an angel had already said in a vision: thou shalt receive. Two men are being moved toward one doorway, and only one of them knows it in advance.

world_behind.title: Verse 31 is written from afterward
world_behind.text: The narrator says they could not be confined in dungeons and no man could slay them, and then notes that they did not use the power until they were bound and imprisoned. He is describing a rescue six chapters before it happens.

words.text: An established practice, the way a thing is usually done. The record uses the noun six times and this is the only place it names a rule about language: settlements take the name of whoever first held them. A writer who normally reports events has stopped to explain how a map gets made.

To listen with intent to obey. The verse says Satan had gotten great hold upon their hearts, therefore they would not hearken. The verb is not about hearing; the chapter has them hearing Alma perfectly well and answering him in detail two verses later.

Abused in words. The sequence in the verse escalates by degrees: withstood all his words, reviled him, spit upon him, cast him out. Speech, then spittle, then the city gate. The record gives each one three or four words and moves on.

Quickly, without delay. He had been thrown out, spat on, and was walking away weighed down with sorrow; the angel speaks, and the next verb is "returned speedily." The adverb is the whole of what the chapter says about his state of mind after the vision.

To give a share of. Amulek uses it of food before he has heard a word of doctrine: I will impart unto thee of my food. The same verb runs through this record for what a church does with its substance, and here it arrives at a private door with bread behind it.

Thick, coarse, grown heavy. "Wax more gross in their iniquities" appears once in scripture. The figure is of something becoming dense. That is a different account of decline than the one the record usually gives.

Underground cells. The word appears twice in this record, and the other is Benjamin telling his people he never suffered them to be confined in one. Here it names what could not hold two men who then let themselves be held anyway.

phrases.term: Many things which cannot be written
phrases.text: The abridger's shrug, and it is unique in scripture. Whatever Alma taught at Gideon beyond the previous chapter is gone. The clause is a reminder that the sermon just read is a selection from something larger, chosen by a man a few hundred years downstream.

phrases.term: After the name of him who first possessed them
phrases.text: A rule about place names, and it makes every settlement in the book a small monument. It also means Ammonihah is somebody's name, which the chapter never mentions again. The rule is given and its application is left to the reader.

phrases.term: Wrestling with God in mighty prayer
phrases.text: Prayer as a physical contest. Enos had opened his book with the wrestle he had before God, and the figure goes back to a man left alone at a ford until daybreak. What Alma is wrestling for is permission to baptize somebody else.

phrases.term: Wading through much tribulation and anguish of soul
phrases.text: Walking through water, slowly, against resistance. It is the second of two uses in scripture and the first belongs to Alma himself, three days unconscious after an angel stopped him. The figure has been kept for the two worst stretches of one man's life.

phrases.term: I am he that delivered it unto you
phrases.text: The angel establishing continuity in six words. Not a message from God in general, but a message from the same messenger, who is now standing on a road twenty years later to tell him to turn around. The sentence makes an errand into a relationship.

phrases.term: He entered the city by another way
phrases.text: Practical, and quietly loaded. He was cast out of Ammonihah; he comes back in by the southern approach. The wise men left Herod by another way for the same kind of reason. Obedience here includes not walking back through the gate that threw you out.

phrases.term: I was about to set my back towards this land forever
phrases.text: An admission to a stranger, in a phrase unique in scripture. He does not say he was discouraged; he says what his body was about to do, and "forever" is his word. The commandment in the next verse is what interrupted it.

phrases.term: They did not exercise their power until they were bound in bands and cast into prison
phrases.text: Power held in reserve on purpose. They could not be confined and could not be killed, and they allowed both to be attempted first. The verse gives the reason plainly: that the Lord might show forth his power in them. That makes the imprisonment part of the demonstration.

verses.label: v. 1–2
verses.title: Home, and the end of a year
verses.text: He comes back from Gideon having taught many things that cannot be written and established the order of the church there as he had at Zarahemla, and goes to his own house to rest from his labors. Then a one-line dateline closing the ninth year.

verses.label: v. 3–6
verses.title: Melek
verses.text: In the tenth year he crosses to the west of Sidon, by the borders of the wilderness, and teaches throughout the land. The people come to him from all the borders and are baptized. When the work is finished he leaves and travels three days north, and arrives at a city called Ammonihah.

verses.label: v. 7–13
verses.title: Ammonihah refuses him
verses.text: The naming custom is explained. He begins to preach; Satan has great hold on their hearts and they will not hearken. He labors in the spirit, wrestling in prayer to be allowed to baptize them. They answer with a legal brief: we know who you are, we are not of your church, you gave up the judgment-seat, you have no power over us. Then they revile him, spit on him, and put him out.

verses.label: v. 14–17
verses.title: The angel
verses.text: Walking toward the city of Aaron, weighed down with sorrow, an angel appears. First: blessed art thou, lift up thy head, rejoice, thou hast been faithful since thy first message, and I am the one who brought it. Then the errand: return, preach again, tell them the Lord will destroy them except they repent. And the reason given is political: they are studying how to destroy the liberty of his people.

verses.label: v. 18–23
verses.title: Back in from the south
verses.text: He returns speedily and comes in from the south. He is hungry and asks a man for food. The man answers that he already knows: an angel said in a vision that he would receive Alma, so come home with me. The man is Amulek. Bread and meat are set out; Alma eats, is filled, blesses the house, and gives thanks.

verses.label: v. 24–27
verses.title: What he tells Amulek
verses.text: Only after eating does he introduce himself as high priest over the church throughout the land, called to preach by the spirit of revelation and prophecy. He says he was cast out and was about to leave for good, and has been commanded to turn back and testify against them. Then the reason he was hungry: he had fasted many days. He stays with Amulek many days before preaching.

verses.label: v. 28–32
verses.title: Sent out together
verses.text: The people grow more gross in their iniquities. The word comes to Alma, and it now includes Amulek by name. Go forth and prophesy, saying repent, or I will visit this people in mine anger. They go out filled with the Holy Ghost, with power that cannot be confined or killed, and they hold it back until they are in prison.

chapter.title: The refusal is legally correct, and that is the point
chapter.text: Ammonihah does not misunderstand Alma; it looks up his jurisdiction and finds he has none. Every word of verse 12 is accurate. The chapter shows a city defeating a prophet on procedure, which is a thing the record has not shown before.

chapter.title: His own best decision becomes their strongest argument
chapter.text: He gave up the bench in order to be able to preach. Ammonihah cites the giving-up as proof he cannot make them listen. The record puts the cost of Alma 4 on the page without commenting on it.

chapter.title: The angel congratulates before it commands
chapter.text: Four clauses of commendation arrive before a single instruction does, and every one of them is about work already finished. A man walking away weighed down with sorrow is told he has done well, and only then told to turn around.

chapter.title: The messenger claims continuity, and it changes the shape of Alma's life
chapter.text: "I am he that delivered it unto you." The angel who stopped him from destroying the church and the angel who sends him back into Ammonihah are the same, which turns two separate episodes into one long assignment with a gap in the middle.

chapter.title: The chapter turns on a meal
chapter.text: A hungry man asks a stranger for food; the stranger has been told to expect him. Alma eats before he introduces himself, before he preaches, before anything. The most consequential partnership in the book begins with bread and meat.

chapter.title: A rejection is weighed on the same scale as his conversion
chapter.text: Mosiah 27 described what Alma went through when the angel stopped him; this verse reuses that description for what he feels walking away from a town. The record is willing to say that being refused cost him something comparable.

chapter.title: Power is described and then deliberately not used
chapter.text: They could not be imprisoned or killed, and they permitted both. The verse states the purpose outright, and in doing so tells the reader six chapters early how Alma 14 ends.

chapter.title: Role in the book
chapter.text: Alma 8 is the hinge of the circuit. Zarahemla was corrected, Gideon was commended, Melek was easy; Ammonihah refuses, and the refusal produces the angel, the return, Amulek, and the eight chapters of confrontation that follow. It also plants the political charge that the war chapters will collect on: they study to destroy the liberty of the people.

applications.title: Expect the successful stop to get four verses
applications.text: Melek worked and the record barely pauses. Most of what goes right in a life will not be the part anyone writes down, including you, and that is not a sign it mattered less.

applications.title: Someone may reject you accurately
applications.text: They had their facts straight and their reasoning was sound. Being right about the procedure and wrong about the substance is a real position, and meeting it requires something other than correcting the record.

applications.title: Commend before you ask for more
applications.text: The angel spends four clauses on what Alma has already done and only then gives the errand. Anyone about to ask a discouraged person for more should notice the order.

applications.title: Go back in by another way
applications.text: He obeyed without walking through the gate that threw him out. Doing the hard thing again does not oblige you to do it identically, and choosing a different approach is not a failure of nerve.

applications.title: Eat first
applications.text: He asked for food before he said who he was. A person who has fasted many days and been spat on is in no state to begin anything, and the chapter treats the meal as the first item of business rather than an interruption to it.

applications.title: Take in the stranger who asks
applications.text: Amulek's whole part in this book starts with him bringing out bread and meat for a hungry man at his door. He had been warned, which most people are not. But what he actually did was feed someone.

applications.title: Hold the power you have
applications.text: They could have walked out of any prison and did not, because the point was not their safety. Capacity withheld on purpose is a different thing from capacity you do not possess, and only one of them is a decision.

questions.text: What am I wrestling for in prayer that is for somebody else and not for me?
Where have I been technically correct and used it to avoid hearing something?
What rejection am I carrying that I have not admitted is grief?
What have I refused to attempt a second time because I would have to go in the same way?
Who has come to my door hungry, and did I ask what they wanted first?
What have I nearly set my back to, forever?
